name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 19 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch's status page, last updated 2 Jun, says the fourth global bleaching event likely ended in 2025 after bleaching-level heat stress reached 84.4% of reef area, and no fifth event has been declared since (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report released on 31 Aug said another event was likely given record sea temperatures and El Niño (bdnews24). Searches on 19 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so Normal holds with an upward trend.
for_you: Reef tourism and reef fisheries are the most exposed. NOAA Coral Reef Watch publishes regional bleaching alerts; a strengthening El Niño raises heat stress risk in the Pacific over the coming months.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress per NOAA Coral Reef Watch (fourth event likely ended 2025)

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching: status update

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
